claims.text: Very selectively, an ophthalmologist may add prednisolone acetate to cut pain and photophobia; contraindicated with HSV keratitis or significant corneal thinning
claims.quote: Very selectively, patients can be treated adjunctively with a glucocorticoid drop (eg, prednisolone acetate). Topical glucocorticoids significantly decrease pain and photophobia, and speed the increase in visual acuity. Because there is a very small risk of the ulcer worsening, adding topical glucocorticoids is only indicated when a patient needs to get back to normal functioning (eg, work, driving) as soon as possible. The final appearance of the scar and final visual acuity may not improve with topical glucocorticoids. Of note, topical glucocorticoids are contraindicated if herpes simplex virus keratitis is suspected or diagnosed, or if there is significant corneal thinning. Such treatment should only be prescribed by ophthalmologists
